intent: H.264 twin of c24-blackout-9s-seq3240: the same 9 s blackout and late frames at 360 packets/s, 3240 sequence numbers, past the jitter buffer's 3000. The buffer takes delta 360 for a new stream and releases it with no loss counted. H.264 has no picture ID, so only the track buffer's follows flag shows the gap: that sample does not follow. The writer requests a key frame, drops deltas 360-377 and resumes at key frame 378, whose PTS must keep the 9.6 s gap. RED when every sample follows, forced in videoSampleOf or ignored by the writer: deltas 360-377 are written (210) with no request. RED: a frame writer that caps a frame step at 1 s, or moves its timestamp on dropped deltas, collapses the gap (timeline). RED: a frame writer that re-bases its timestamp at a sequence jump of 3000 or more plays key frame 378 9 s early (timeline). h264-c24-blackout-9s-seq2160 passes that mutation, so the pair tells the two paths apart. RED: a frame writer that takes the arrival gap for a step of over 3 s misplaces key frame 378 (timeline).
